PhD Overview

  • University: Monash University
  • Department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
  • Location: Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
  • Study Level: PhD / Doctoral Research
  • Project Title: Smart Polymer Nanocomposites: Design, Synthesis and Applications
  • Research Area: Polymer Science, Materials Science, Nanotechnology and Nanocomposites
  • Duration: Approximately 3.5 years
  • Funding: Fully funded PhD scholarship
  • Supervisor: Associate Professor Vipul Agarwal
  • International Applicants: Eligible subject to Monash University admission and scholarship requirements
  • Application Status: Applicants should confirm current project and scholarship availability with the supervisor and Monash University before applying.

About the Research Project

The PhD project focuses on the design and development of smart polymer nanocomposites for advanced coating and foam applications.

A major challenge in conventional polymer nanocomposites is achieving effective and controlled dispersion of fillers throughout the polymer matrix. The research will investigate new synthesis approaches for developing polymeric and multidimensional filler nanocomposites with controlled structures and tunable properties.

Particular attention will be given to controlling the interfacial arrangement of multidimensional fillers around polymer particles, including systems formed in oil-water emulsions.

The project will also investigate externally stimuli-responsive polymer nanocomposite coatings and foams.

Potential applications include:

  • sensing technologies;
  • chemical catalysis;
  • corrosion protection;
  • shielding materials;
  • smart coatings; and
  • functional polymer foam technologies.

The work combines polymer science, nanomaterials, surface and interface chemistry, materials synthesis and advanced materials characterisation.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly relevant to applicants with an academic or research background in areas such as:

  • Chemistry;
  • Polymer Chemistry;
  • Materials Science;
  • Materials Engineering;
  • Nanotechnology;
  • Polymer Science; or
  • closely related disciplines.

Candidates are expected to demonstrate strong academic performance and research potential.

Relevant laboratory experience may include:

  • polymer synthesis;
  • nanoparticle synthesis;
  • nanocomposite fabrication;
  • materials characterisation;
  • polymer or nanoparticle analytical techniques; and
  • experimental materials research.

Strong scientific writing skills and the ability to conduct research independently and collaboratively are also valuable.

Peer-reviewed research publications, particularly strong first-author publications, may make an applicant more competitive, although applicants must ultimately satisfy Monash University's formal admission and scholarship criteria.

Monash University PhD Entry Requirements

For standard PhD admission, Monash University normally requires one of the following:

  • a relevant bachelor's degree of at least four years that includes a research thesis or research project, with results equivalent to at least Australian Second Class Honours Division A (2A);
  • a relevant master's degree containing a substantial research thesis or project equivalent to at least 25% of one year of full-time study, with results equivalent to at least Second Class Honours Division A; or
  • another qualification and relevant experience considered equivalent by Monash University's Graduate Research Committee.

Meeting the minimum PhD admission requirements does not automatically guarantee a scholarship. Research scholarships at Monash are competitive and take into account academic achievement, research experience and research outputs.

English Language Requirements

International applicants must satisfy Monash University's graduate research English language proficiency requirements.

Evidence may be provided through an approved English-language test or, in eligible cases, previous tertiary education undertaken entirely in English.

Applicants should check the current Monash Graduate Research English Language Proficiency requirements before submitting their application because accepted tests, score requirements and validity conditions may change.

Scholarship and Funding

The advertised project has been promoted as a fully funded 3.5-year PhD opportunity.

For centrally managed Monash graduate research scholarships, the standard 2026 RTP Stipend and Monash Graduate Scholarship rate is AUD $37,145 per year for full-time students.

Depending on the scholarship awarded, funding may include:

  • a living allowance/stipend;
  • relocation allowance where applicable; and
  • tuition-fee support for eligible students.

For international students, Monash also offers tuition scholarships that may be packaged with a stipend scholarship. The Monash International Tuition Scholarship can cover course tuition fees and a single Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) policy.

Applicants should note that the exact funding package attached to an individual research project must be confirmed with Monash University or the project supervisor.

Supervisor

The project is associated with Associate Professor Vipul Agarwal in the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Monash University.

His research profile lists the following PhD projects:

  • Smart polymer nanocomposites: design, synthesis and applications
  • Sustainable recycled three-dimensional polymer nanocomposites

His Monash University profile currently indicates that he is accepting PhD students.

How to Apply

Applicants should first review the project and contact the prospective supervisor where required by the Faculty of Engineering.

A typical Monash graduate research application involves:

  1. checking eligibility for the PhD program;
  2. identifying and contacting an appropriate research supervisor;
  3. preparing the required research and academic documentation;
  4. providing evidence of English-language proficiency;
  5. obtaining a faculty invitation to apply where required; and
  6. submitting the PhD and scholarship application through Monash University's graduate research application system.

Graduate research admission and scholarship applications are normally submitted through the Monash myApp portal.

Eligible applicants applying through the central graduate research scholarship process are automatically considered for applicable Monash graduate research scholarships rather than having to submit a separate application for every scholarship.

Documents Typically Required

Applicants should prepare relevant documents such as:

  • academic transcripts;
  • degree certificates;
  • curriculum vitae (CV);
  • research proposal where required;
  • evidence of previous research experience;
  • publications or research outputs where applicable;
  • English-language proficiency evidence;
  • scholarship or sponsorship documentation where relevant; and
  • any additional documents requested by the university.
